stores.store_id: Unique alphanumeric identifier for each retail store (primary key, format: S##)
stores.store_name: Human-readable display name of the retail store location
stores.region: High-level geographic sales region grouping (e.g., Northeast, Southeast) — 4 distinct regions across 10 stores
stores.city: City in which the store is physically located — 10 unique cities, one per store
stores.state: US state abbreviation for the store location — 9 unique states across 10 stores

sales_data.transaction_id: Unique transaction identifier — prefix TXN= sale, RET= return/refund; 5% null rate and potential duplicate detected; primary key integrity at risk
sales_data.transaction_date: Date on which the transaction occurred — stored as raw string in mixed formats (MM/DD/YYYY and YYYY-MM-DD); requires normalisation before use
sales_data.store_id: Foreign key referencing stores.store_id — identifies the store where the transaction occurred; 10% null rate means 2 of 20 transactions are unattributable to a store
sales_data.product_id: Foreign key referencing products.product_id — identifies the product transacted; fully populated, 10 distinct products appear in transactions
sales_data.product_name: Denormalised product display name copied from the product catalog — redundant with products.product_name; should be resolved via join in Silver layer
sales_data.category: Denormalised product category copied from the product catalog — contains dirty/abbreviated values (e.g., 'Elec.' vs 'Electronics'); 13 unique values vs 5 canonical values in products.category
sales_data.quantity: Number of units sold or returned in the transaction — negative values indicate return/refund records; range -2 to 8
sales_data.unit_price: Price per unit charged at time of transaction — ranges from $0.01 to $9,999.99; extreme outliers suspected; may deviate from products.standard_price
sales_data.total_amount: Total monetary value of the transaction (quantity × unit_price) — negative values confirm return records; range -$387.64 to $9,999.99
sales_data.customer_segment: Customer loyalty/value tier classification at time of transaction — contains abbreviation inconsistencies (e.g., 'Prem' vs 'Premium'); 9 unique values suggest dirty data
sales_data.payment_method: Payment instrument used for the transaction — 4 distinct methods: Apple Pay, PayPal, Debit Card, and at least one other

products.product_id: Unique alphanumeric identifier for each product in the catalog (primary key, format: P###) — 20 unique values, fully clean
products.product_name: Official product display name as defined in the master catalog — 20 unique, fully populated
products.category: Canonical product category classification — 5 distinct categories; authoritative source for resolving dirty category values in sales_data
products.standard_price: Official list/catalog price for the product — range $12.99 to $999.99; serves as reference baseline for validating sales_data.unit_price deviations

quality_notes: sales_data.transaction_id has a 5% null rate (1 of 20 rows) and only 18 unique values across 20 rows, indicating a missing primary key and a likely duplicate record — primary key constraint cannot be enforced without remediation

sales_data.store_id has a 10% null rate (2 of 20 rows), meaning 2 transactions cannot be joined to the stores dimension — these records will be lost in any INNER JOIN and must be handled explicitly (default store, reject queue, or NULL-safe LEFT JOIN)

sales_data.transaction_date is stored as a raw string with mixed date formats (MM/DD/YYYY and YYYY-MM-DD across 17 unique values) — must be parsed and normalised to ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) before Bronze-to-Silver promotion

sales_data.category contains 13 unique values versus 5 canonical categories in products.category — dirty values identified include abbreviations such as 'Elec.' instead of 'Electronics'; a category lookup/standardisation map is required in the Silver transformation
sales_data.customer_segment contains 9 unique values suggesting abbreviation variants (e.g., 'Prem' vs 'Premium') — a segment standardisation lookup table should be applied during cleansing

sales_data.quantity has a minimum value of -2 and sales_data.total_amount has a minimum of -387.64, confirming return/refund transactions are co-mingled with sales records (identified by 'RET' prefix in transaction_id) — Silver layer should split or flag these as a separate transaction_type dimension

sales_data.unit_price ranges from $0.01 to $9,999.99 while products.standard_price ranges from $12.99 to $999.99 — the 10x upper discrepancy and near-zero lower bound indicate potential data entry errors or test records; a price variance threshold check should be implemented

sales_data.product_name and sales_data.category are denormalised columns that duplicate information available in the products dimension — these should be dropped from the Silver fact table and resolved via join to products on product_id to ensure single source of truth
stores dataset is fully clean: no nulls across all 5 columns, all primary keys unique, consistent formatting throughout — safe to load as-is to Bronze and Silver

products dataset is fully clean: no nulls across all 4 columns, all 20 product_id values are unique — safe to load as-is; standard_price should serve as the authoritative price reference for downstream margin and discount calculations
